reviews.title: Inaccessible for blind user, but great idea… Wish I could use it
reviews.text: I hate writing negative reviews. I almost never do it. Honestly, I rarely write reviews in general, but I’d much rather write positive ones. And frankly, I think this is an amazing app and a really necessary and awesome concept. I’m a mental health counseling of recommended this app to a lot of my clients… But I can’t use it myself. I am blind, and the app is so inaccessible that I can’t even find where to give feedback privately in the app. Honestly, I wish I could just email the developers and send feedback through the app so I wouldn’t have to post this publicly, but the is so accessible I can’t do that. So… I’m hoping very much at the developers will see this and take steps to make their app accessible for blind users like myself. Please test your app with mobile device screen readers like Apple‘s built-in voiceover so that I can use it. If you do that, I will happily change this review to five stars and absolutely gush about it. This is a cry for help, not an attempt to tear this thing down. It’s awesome and it should be better and more accessible. Looking forward to changing this review. I will check in on the app every couple of weeks for a while to see if anything gets better. Looking forward to that.

It’s so helpful to join the live sessions! Sometimes I join just long enough to get started or get up. Other times I join for the whole session! I love how involved the hosts are as well as how welcoming everyone is - both on the app and in the FB group. Through Dubbii I have found the support I always needed but didn’t know could exist!!! 

I highly recommend this app if you struggle to complete daily tasks, whether that’s hygiene related, cleaning, etc.

reviews.title: Use it all the time
reviews.text: I’ve had this app for almost a year now and I still use it regularly. On hard days I’ll join every live body doubling session available and it really helps get me through the things I absolutely do not want to do at all. Such a supportive, positive, and realistic community, and authentic people. I recommend this app, and especially the live body doubling sessions, to everyone. It takes a session or two to get used to the hosts saying supportive things in the background; it was initially distracting but it rarely takes me out of the zone now. There’s also pre-recorded body doubling videos for all kinds of tasks that I use sometimes as well. The live sessions are especially helpful if you’re having a lot of negative feelings about yourself or whatever you’re struggling with. They’re great for making you feel “ok” when you don’t. Can’t say enough good things, I love this app.

This app has seriously helped me so much, I can’t thank Rox and Rich and the entire Dubbii team enough. I’m autistic and have chronic/treatment-resistant depression, and taking care of myself and my home is often really difficult overwhelming. Having follow-along videos and especially the live sessions helps me so much to ensure that I will at least get *something* done every day. I am beyond grateful for this app for helping me take care of myself. 

In the future, I’d love it if the follow along videos had some talking/chatter to give my brain something to listen to! Doesn’t have to be anything super important or meaningful, but I love listening to chitchat while I’m getting stuff done (that’s part of the reason I love the live sessions so much!) 

I’d also love it if the social media group could move to Discord or something similar that doesn’t rely on having a Facebook/Meta account to participate!

reviews.title: Unique idea getting ruined
reviews.text: This app has been very helpful for me for a while. Unfortunately the live sessions are becoming something different than what I was hoping. The focus has become much more about individuals putting attention on themselves instead of everyone contentedly working alongside each other. Many people are spending the time just typing in chat and requesting to speak to the group and getting individualized support from the host. At the end, everyone is supposed to share their "ta-da" list but you're lucky to have it read over everyone vying for special attention. I feel frustrated and alienated after sessions anymore, because they seem to revolve around whoever clamours the loudest instead of the group as a whole. If you're just quietly doing your thing, the experience is more like listening in on someone else's group call while you work. Apparently this is the direction that's popular, but popular rarely goes hand-in-hand with great and original ideas.

reviews.title: The ADHD App that WORKS
reviews.text:
Just coming in for a thankful moment! 

TL:DR: Dubbi has been so helpful, and has helped me with internal self talk more than I thought anything possibly could. 

My Experience so far: 

After lurking for a while watching Rox and Ricky on Youtube, I found myself back in ADHD burn out or closely approaching it. I started therapy and slowly the weight fell off, and unfortunately as we unpacked while building coping skills I felt that weight build back up. We were at a point where scheduled vacation turned into a longer vacation and sick time because daily panic attacks for hours are not friendly to anyone, and even less so to connective tissue disorder folx. 

So at the same time my homework was to “Be Kind to Yourself”, I found Dubbii. At first, the external structure was a support in itself as I tried to figure out if this would work for me. Then it turned into peaceful anchors to my day, and slowly my internal scripts started rewriting themselves. The “author experience” of this process is still underway but is honestly more improved than I could have hoped for. Now after over a month or so of the sessions my own voice kindly reminds me to care and “be nicer to myself and others”. Instead of doom spiraling, Mariah’s Coconut Mall starts to play, and the anxious thoughts get noticed with Nicki’s “Oh I hope you are okay, we are here for you” with my own kind of spin to it. More noticeably two very mild panics attacks in that timeframe, down from daily when starting. In 6 weeks! 

On top of this, doom piles were cleaned, cabinets organized, work was more manageable, I gained more of a sense of community, and feel better. While there’s still work to be done, “thats okay we are gonna roll it over to the next day” and it’s more doable with Dubbii. 

While medication and professional help cannot replace Dubbii, it IS an amazing add on to the full self care toolbox. Both my therapist and psychiatry providers have it as a shareable option now with their clients after my experience and I am so glad this exists. 

Thank you! And see ya at the next session!

reviews.title: Great for body doubling
reviews.text: This is a great app for body doubling. You can use the videos where they take you step-by-step through tasks like how to make a bed, etc.,   You can also use the live one hour Zoom sessions. This is where you have one coordinator Who reads chat messages and respond to us. There are also a whole bunch of people doing things on camera and you can choose to body double with each other. But you don’t have to get on camera if you don’t want to. The organizers are very responsive to the needs of the community. I live in the US and they started with sessions that were centered around UK daytimes. But they have some more sessions and I can attend the 3pm (my time) one. It is a pretty new app and they are still evolving. I suggest everyone try this and see if it works for them.

reviews.title: A lot better than you think
reviews.text:
I heard about the app from social media videos. At first I had my doubts - a lot of the videos go by really quickly and it almost looked like, at first, a lot of the tasks that were being taken on were not as overwhelming as the ones I was struggling with. I felt very ashamed and was wondering if this was not for me. Let alone, the live body doubling sessions could be overwhelming at times. 

 Then I realized - in the prerecorded videos - Roxanne and Rich deal with different workloads that are appropriate for neurotypical and neurodivergent people. A great example of this is their de cluttering videos. While Roxanne deals with an overwhelming closet / wash room, Rich is dealing with a larger room. I was feeling a lot less ashamed - they are dealing with the same amount of struggle but Roxanne is trying to balance something more manageable. 

 The messy mode videos are the ones that struck home with being the most relatable and had me feeling the most comfortable. Rather than individual steps or a short body doubling video, these are your long videos with some sections you can jump between. Seeing the mess helped me feel a lot less ashamed because it was what I was dealing with at the time. The step by step instructions were great. 

 One of the ideal videos I like with a timer is the study time one. I love that it has background noise and it’s working in complete silence otherwise. I wish we had more videos like that. I still think that some of the timed videos are a little too fast for me - I work best without shorter timers. And the live body doubling gets a lot to get used to - because I feel like I have to respond or be on camera. But honestly - if you say nothing and keep it in the background it works really well. 

 Plus - since they’re based in the UK - there’s a lot here for those of us who use other body doubling that only has morning or afternoon slots. This allows a lot of great work to be done for night owls in the US. Overall, if you are looking for a rather cheap subscription app that works decently for body doubling and background noise - this is very solid. 

I use it on top of another ADHD app for coaching / body doubling. It will not replace a coach - but those coaching sessions are expensive and this gets you by.

Update: The only suggestions I would have is being able to register with another email so that I can switch between my Android phone and iPad without having to pay a subscription twice. Plus, I would love a website version! Looking forward to seeing any new body doubling videos I saw from Developer replies, and more fun things with body doubling. 

Thank you for a wonderful new community to be part of and helping us feel not ashamed - and proud of how much we’ve accomplished!

With that being said, I did have a problem with the nudges. While I appreciate the PDA mode (it made me laugh when I saw it), and the many choices for sounds, I wish there was a way to repeat it. When I first saw the task, I (stupidly) decided I would do it later, then never did. If the nudge had an ability to repeat when it notices I didn’t press “done”, that would be fantastic!

So far this app has been really helpful, this is the only flaw I foresee and really the only thing keeping me from the subscription!

reviews.title: This is a LIFE SAVING app!!!
reviews.text:
You guys are absolutely incredible. I've been using dubbii for several months now and the way it has entirely changed my headspace when it comes to doing necessary (but often not fun) tasks is remarkable. 

Firstly, it's like having someone there with you doing the task. As someone who lives alone, this has had such a positive impact. I'm often embarrassed at how messy my space can become when I don't have the bandwidth to stay on top of things, so the prospect of inviting a friend over to body double while I clean is a vulnerable, intimidating thing. With dubbii, there's zero fear of judgement. 

Additionally, each task is marked with a time estimate. I didn't realise how helpful this was until a few months in, but part of my dread of starting tasks has to do with the amount of time I *think* it's going to take in my head. When I see that the washing up is only going to take 10-20 minutes, I don't drag my feet to start. It seems like a surmountable task.

Another thing I love is the ability to choose who to follow along with. Roxy's videos are always fun and full of energy, while Rich's videos are very calming and methodical, so you can choose based on your own personality or current mood/vibe. They both have a way of making you feel unjudged, while proving that each task is really not as big and scary as your brain has made it out to be.

The option to choose just a simple body doubling video with no instructions (for those times when you don't want to be told what to do) or a step by step guide to the task (for the times when you don't have enough spoons to remember what comes next) is also *majorly* helpful. 

They have a "make a suggestion" button at the bottom of the task video list. I suggested a packing tutorial a few months ago and took a short break from using the app, and I see now they've made videos for packing! Whether it was my suggestion they took, multiple of the same suggestion, or something they'd already planned to do, it seems like they have new tasks and features coming out consistently, and I love that they are interested in listening to what the users want/need.

Thank you so so much for this app guys!! 🖤✨

reviews.title: Dubbii is SO SMART!!😃
reviews.text: I have been using dubbii for a while and I really think that this is the best thing for me. I have ADHD and my psychiatrist has always assumed that I also have autism but I’ve never been tested for autism anyway I have a terrible time concentrating on doing every day tasks and until I found this wonderful couple, I had no idea that body doubling was a thing. I used to drag my husband into every room with me and just sit there so that I could do every day tasks that seemed really hard. My husband also has ADHD but he is very unaware of how it affects him on a day-to-day basis, and he cannot sit still and he constantly paces. It’s really hard for him to be a body double person for me. Sometimes I have to pay him two dollars to get him to stay with me for 20 minutes. I mean, whatever works right. But now that I have this app, I don’t need to drag him with me into every room. Now I can just watch Rox and Rich do everything that I need to get done and it helps me focus immensely. I am so glad that they created it and Without it I would be lost. I cannot explain how grateful I am to the both of you for thinking of all of us in the world, who need help. For people who don’t understand it might seem like a simple thing to make the bed but it can take me eight hours. Sometimes it takes me all day to make the bed and then when I finally do make the bed it’s time to go to bed, and then I never feel accomplished. I would rate this app 10 out of 10 stars. I love it so much and YOU should download it too because it will really change your life. Love to both Rich and Rox. ❤️ ❤️ ❤️

reviews.title: Ideas!
reviews.text: I have only just begun to use this app and I am loving it. I have not been able to stop coming up with ideas and wanted to share in hopes it eventually gets incorporated. would love for each task to have a low energy and high energy version so that there feels like more of an option if i need to do more of the bare minimum. Like for cleaning if there is a definitely do this to avoid mold, nasty smells etc to other times when i want to clean out my fridge. i think it would be fun if deeper cleaning things were suggested as bonus items and get points for doing them. it would make them feel less like a chore. it would also be cool if there was a note taking portion of the app to store thoughts about chores or tasks but you don’t necessarily want to be a nudge. I was also thinking about if there was a way for users to create custom tasks that let’s say i have a specific task to do, i could break down the steps and have it stored in the app as a task i could complete many times over, yea it wouldn’t have the body doubling portion but i think it would be useful itself. i think a fun thing to add to the body doubling portion is if it showed you how many people had that task open , don’t have to show who it is (although if you had friends on it and could see what one of your friends was working on or struggling on and sending a message or some interactive feature). thinking about if there is a way for when i first grab my phone in the morning it would open the morning routine (or another task) making me more inclined to go ahead and get up and do it. i know this is a lot but it’s been making me think a lot about how we can use social media to our advantage instead of doom scrolling all the time.  even if only one of these things happened i’d be so happy. some im sure are more complicated than others and ive never built an app but just an excited adhd person wanting to get everything i can out of an amazing app.

reviews.title: Breath of air
reviews.text:
Hopefully an example that will land for the folks that are debating using this app. 

I grew up in a relatively day-to-day unsteady environment when most kids would be learning consistency for cleaning their room or developing good hygiene habits, etc. I didn’t get that. I knew brushing my teeth was necessary but ya just throw the toothpaste on a brush and call it good, right? Nope, ya gotta floss, and brush, and use mouthwash; at least that’s what was always preached but never taught to me. To some this may seem stupidly simple but it wasn’t and as I got older the potential embarrassment grew, how can I be in my late teens then early twenties then late twenties without having a routine for brushing my teeth?

I’ve never had an “easy” time at the dentist and I always dreaded it every time because it was painful but I had to deal with it. After using this app and getting off to a running start with the teeth brushing video, I may not brush my teeth every night but I. Have. A. Routine. I now know how it feels to have my teeth and mouth clean on a daily basis. And ya know what? Not 4 months brushing my teeth like I learned with the app and I had the EASIEST dental cleaning in my life! As it turns out, doing those things regularly and accurately makes the preventative appointments so much better. I walked out of the building feeling accomplished and so ‘adult’ and now brushing my teeth is a habit I have always wanted and never had. Without this app, I don’t know if that would have been as possible. 

To anyone debating, give it a shot. Try the free videos and you’ll know whether you want it or not, I will say it has been an absolute saving grace.

reviews.title: Missing the point
reviews.text:
A video tutorial maybe? But this is not body doubling. Who ever made these videos is kind of missing the point of body doubling. The videos are short, with the steps described rather than acted out for a lot of them. These videos are SHORT, like 15 seconds. You cannot watch these videos while doing the tasks at all. 

I started with room clean, their room is spotless, only like 2 cups and a small piece of trash. So naturally it takes her 20 seconds to pick up all trash. This is completely unrealistic for 90% of ND individuals. The whole point of the word ‘doubling’ implies we are doing the same thing at the same time. This is just a paid video of someone saying ‘pick up your trash’ and then you having to do it on your own. Don’t bother.

reviews.title: Validation: showers are exhausting
reviews.text:
I thought I was the only one that hated showers but took them as often as I could force my self.  Sure, taking out the trash and room of doom is awesome and I have definitely used those videos.  But the one that I keep coming back to is the shower.  When I heard Rox say ‘so much effort showering’ (for the first time), I thought ‘I’m not the only one!   

Other things I like: 
There are two styles of doubling. I tend towards Rox, because she has ADHD and reminds us of things that I seem to always forget (get the towel and put on deodorant). Rich is also great. 
I love that I feel like they are having conversations with me as they go along. (Except in the shower, that’s quiet). 
I love the celebration at the end and the badges. 

Also, as a plug for their content, they explain things so well.  I feel like Rox explains it the way I’m thinking, then Rich explains it how I would like to but can’t articulate it to non-ADHDers.  And I thank you! This late diagnosis adhd mom with her adhd son loves you all the way from the US in South Carolina! 

Thank you for taking a chance and opening up!!!

reviews.title: Love the Concept, need Larger Screen Capabilities
reviews.text: I’ve just opened the app (after having downloaded it a month ago and then forgetting I had it) and so far I love the concept and 90% of the execution. But where there’s a huge disconnect for me is that when I, say, call a friend to body double they’ll usually talk to me while I complete a task, and so while my brain is occupied in listening and trying to answer a conversation my body is able to take care of tasks. I get this isn’t practical for the app, but then I miss out on the other part of body doubling which is having someone in the room with you. The body doubling screen is so brilliant, but so small — I find myself needing to hold my phone to trick my brain, but then I just end up doom scrolling. An app for a smart TV might be too big of an ask, but a way to “cast” or “stream” the body doubling footage to my TV would be so helpful because as Rox works, I can work. Anyways — I really recommend anyone to just try the app out once, my problems might not be the same as yours, and the concept is so, so cool. Thank you!

reviews.title: Holding back tears of relief!
reviews.text:
Thank you guys SO MUCH for making this app!

 Changing the sheets was the free chore I chose. I followed Rox as she broke it all down step by step. I felt my relief increase each step through because I stayed on task and did not have to make the “simple” (super difficult for me) decisions. I also felt less and less shame and isolation with each comment Rox made about it being hard, difficult, or down right life sucking!

reviews.title: There for me.
reviews.text: This app is a great addition to the scaffolding I’ve built in my life to help me navigate the challenges of ADHD. I’m so glad to have it. I couldn’t get my yearly subscription fast enough! Thank you for making dubbii. It started helping me right away.

reviews.title: Simple, Effective and Gives Me Hope
reviews.text: I lose track so easily and to have people by your side helping you truly makes a difference. Thanks for this app!

reviews.title: Genius!!!
reviews.text: Just subscribed to the app and will be screaming from the rooftops how friggen GENIUS it is! The break in between videos so you don’t find yourself down a rabbit hole of just watching someone else clean is so smart and helpful. Both Rich & Rox are a delight to listen to. Easy to use & follow along with, idk genius is truly the only word I can think of to describe it.

reviews.title: Love it
reviews.text: I’m so glad they has come out with this app and I love the option of breaking down each step or just playing the video with music, so I have someone doing it along with me!

reviews.title: What my 39 yo Executive ADHD brain DESP NEEDED!
